@graph.articleBody: If you clean homes, fix pipes or mow lawns, your customers never visit your office. You go to them. That creates a problem the moment you set up a Google Business Profile: the form asks for an address, and the address you have is your house, your garage or a P.O. box. This guide walks you through the setup the way Google describes it. You will decide whether you are a service area business, hide your address if you should, choose your service areas, and avoid the setup mistakes that put a profile at risk. Key

itemListElement.name: How to Set Up a Google Business Profile for a Service Area Business

mainEntity.name: Should a service area business hide its address on Google?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Google says that if you are a service area business, you should hide your business address from customers. If you do not serve customers at your business address, Google says to remove it from your Business Profile.

mainEntity.name: How many service areas can I add to my Google Business Profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says you can set up to 20 service areas, based on the cities, postal codes or other areas you serve. Choose the places where you actually take jobs.

mainEntity.name: How far can my service area extend?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says a service area shouldn't extend farther than about 2 hours of driving time from where your business is based. Google's pages do not say that a bigger area makes you appear more often.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a P.O. box or virtual office as my business address?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says P.O. boxes or mailboxes located at remote locations aren't acceptable, and that a rented mailing address where you do not operate isn't eligible for a Business Profile.

Google defines it as a business that serves customers at its business address but also directly visits or delivers to them. These businesses can show their storefront address and designate a service area.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to verify my service area business?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Google says you need to verify your business to edit your business info and interact with customers. The verification method is determined by Google and can't be changed.

mainEntity.name: Can I create a separate profile for each city I serve?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says not to create more than one page for each location of your business. A service area business should have one profile for its base, with a designated service area.
